s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with inflammatory infiltrate and history of local excisions and immunotherapy
salient_findings: New and progressive satellite lesions despite pembrolizumab therapy
Multiple unresectable satellite lesions after ipilimumab treatment
Intense mixed superficial and deep dermal inflammatory infiltrate
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 50s
Initial treatment was wide local excision with graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion
Incidentally resected lymph node was found to be focally involved
No evidence of distant metastatic disease initially
Multiple satellite lesions appeared within months after initial treatment
Patient received 4 cycles of ipilimumab
Second wide local excision was performed when new lesions appeared
Pembrolizumab therapy was started after additional satellite lesions developed
Local progression occurred in satellite lesions after 5 cycles of pembrolizumab
Histopathology showed intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
Immunostaining results highlighted normal melanocytes, histiocytes, and neutrophils

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of melanoma, with initial treatment involving wide local excision and graft repair for a left posterior auricular scalp lesion, and subsequent development of satellite lesions

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with progressive skin lesions and a history of immunotherapy, which could be related to cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of lymph node involvement and development of new lesions, which could be indicative of cutaneous B-cell lymphoma

shortlist.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with aggressive skin lesions and a history of immunotherapy, which could be related to Merkel cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of local excisions and development of new lesions, which could be indicative of angiosarcoma

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a scalp lesion, focal lymph node involvement, and development of satellite lesions, along with histopathology showing intense mixed inflammatory infiltrate and immunostaining results highlighting normal melanocytes, are consistent with melanoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Lack of specific histopathological features and immunophenotyping characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: No evidence of B-cell lymphoma specific markers or histological features

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: No mention of characteristic Merkel cell carcinoma histological features or immunostaining patterns

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: No indication of vascular tumor characteristics or specific immunohistochemical markers for angiosarcoma

gold: Stage IIIC (T4aN3) melanoma with satellite metastases
